answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token before posting jobs or claiming rewards. An attacker may generate thousands of keys, but each needs its own deposit; proven fraud slashes the stake to compensate victims. Reputation accrues only through verified work, so splitting one record across fresh accounts gains little. The attacker pays in tied-up capital and lost deposits, not just the cost of making keys. Names like nectar, opal, and echo grant no exemption.
